stories.headline: Anthropic Launches 'Dreaming' for Claude Managed Agents, Enabling Self-Improvement Between Sessions

key_facts.fact: Anthropic launched 'dreaming' as a research preview in Claude Managed Agents — a scheduled process that reviews past agent sessions and memory stores, extracts patterns, and curates memories so agents improve over time.

Dreaming surfaces patterns a single agent can't see, including recurring mistakes, workflows agents converge on, and team-wide preferences; users can choose automatic memory updates or review changes first.

Anthropic also made 'outcomes' generally available — a feature where a rubric-based grader evaluates agent output in a separate context window and the agent self-corrects, improving task success by up to 10 points over standard prompting.

Multiagent orchestration was also made broadly available, allowing a lead agent to delegate subtasks to specialist agents with separate context windows and tools, while maintaining a shared memory store.

The features were announced at Anthropic's Code with Claude developer conference in San Francisco, where CEO Dario Amodei said the company could grow by 80x in 2026 and its growth rate is 'too hard to handle.'

stories.headline: Anthropic Signs Deal for All of SpaceX's Colossus 1 Capacity, Doubles Claude Code Rate Limits

key_facts.fact: Anthropic signed an agreement with SpaceX to use all of the compute capacity at the Colossus 1 data center in Memphis, gaining access to more than 300 MW of new capacity (over 220,000 NVIDIA GPUs including H100, H200, and GB200 accelerators) within the month.

Anthropic doubled Claude Code's five-hour rate limits for Pro, Max, Team, and seat-based Enterprise plans, removed the peak hours limit reduction on Claude Code for Pro and Max accounts, and raised API rate limits considerably for Claude Opus models — all effective May 6.

Anthropic also expressed interest in partnering with SpaceX to develop multiple gigawatts of orbital AI compute capacity, as compute required for next-generation systems is outpacing terrestrial power, land, and cooling.

The deal adds to Anthropic's existing compute portfolio: up to 5 GW agreement with Amazon (nearly 1 GW by end of 2026), 5 GW deal with Google and Broadcom (starting 2027), $30B Microsoft-NVIDIA Azure partnership, and $50B US AI infrastructure investment with Fluidstack.

Elon Musk reversed his stance on Anthropic after spending time with senior members last week, saying 'No one set off my evil detector' — having called Anthropic 'misanthropic and evil' as recently as February.

The deal gives IPO-bound SpaceX a marquee AI customer weeks before its planned public listing targeting a $1.75T–$2T valuation, with the public S-1 expected by late May and roadshow set for the week of June 8.

Anthropic's surging demand has been driven partly by users moving away from OpenAI after military contract controversy, increasing adoption of Claude Code in professional software development, and a shift from single-agent chat to multi-agent workflows.

stories.headline: Arm Q4 Revenue Up 20% to Record $1.49B; AGI CPU Demand Doubles to $2B as Datacenter Nears Top Business

key_facts.fact: Arm reported Q4 FY2026 revenue of $1.49B, up 20% YoY, with licensing revenue up 29% to $819M and royalty revenue up 11% to $671M. Non-GAAP EPS was a record $0.60.
Full-year FY2026 revenue reached a record $4.92B, up 23% YoY, with non-GAAP EPS of $1.77 for the year.
Customer demand for the Arm AGI CPU, launched in March, has doubled to more than $2B across FY2027 and FY2028, up from $1B stated at launch. Meta is the lead partner.
Data center royalties more than doubled YoY for the second consecutive year. CEO Rene Haas said datacenter will 'soon' be Arm's largest business.
Cerebras, OpenAI, Positron, and Rebellions are integrating the Arm AGI CPU alongside accelerator-based systems. Commercial systems are now available from ASRock, Lenovo, Quanta, and Supermicro.
Arm warned of phone market weakness, with CEO Haas saying unit growth 'flip to negative' last quarter, concentrated in the lower end.
Q1 FY2027 guidance: revenue of ~$1.26B (up ~20% YoY) and non-GAAP EPS of $0.40. Shares swung widely, dropping ~6% after hours on softer-than-expected guidance.

stories.headline: China Invokes Blocking Statute for First Time, Bans Firms from Complying with US Sanctions

key_facts.fact: On May 2, China's Ministry of Commerce publicly barred companies from complying with US sanctions after the US blacklisted five Chinese refineries for processing Iranian oil — the first time China has invoked its so-called blocking statute.
Iran's FM Abbas Araghchi met China's Wang Yi in Beijing on May 6 — his first visit since the war started on Feb 28 — to coordinate ahead of the Trump-Xi summit scheduled for May 14-15.
Wang Yi called for a 'comprehensive ceasefire' and said China hopes relevant parties will respond to calls from the international community to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

China accounted for up to 90% of Iran's oil exports before the war, importing over 1 million barrels per day. The blocking statute enables refiners to continue processing Iranian crude that arrives outside the US blockade area.
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said China's continued purchases of Iranian oil amounted to 'funding global terrorism.'

stories.headline: AI Insurance Startup Corgi Raises $160M Series B at $1.3B Valuation, Becomes YC's Latest Unicorn

key_facts.fact: Corgi, an AI-native full-stack insurance startup for startups, raised $160 million in Series B funding at a $1.3 billion valuation, led by TCV — becoming Y Combinator's latest unicorn.
The round comes just four months after Corgi's $108 million across seed and Series A; total funding to date exceeds $268 million, with investors including YC, Kindred Ventures, and Contrary.
Founded by Emily Yuan and Nico Laqua in 2024 (YC Spring 2024 batch), Corgi uses AI systems to power underwriting, claims, and policy operations; customers include Deel and Artisan.
Corgi is expanding into new verticals beginning with trucking, and plans to move into payroll and small business insurance, automating workflows across the real economy.

Corgi recently launched AI Insurance Coverage that integrates directly with existing tech E&O policies, offering modular coverage for AI-related risks including biased algorithms, harmful generated content, and autonomous system failures.

stories.headline: Pancreatic Cancer Drug Daraxonrasib Doubles Survival in Phase 3, Results Published in NEJM

key_facts.fact: Phase 3 trial results showed patients receiving daraxonrasib plus chemotherapy had overall survival of 13.2 months vs 6.7 months for chemotherapy alone — nearly double.

Phase 1/2 results published on May 6 in the New England Journal of Medicine showed daraxonrasib stopped tumors from progressing for over 8 months and kept patients alive for up to nearly 18 months in 168 patients with advanced metastatic disease.
Daraxonrasib targets the RAS protein — mutated in over 90% of pancreatic cancers — long considered 'undruggable.' It works by pairing with cyclophilin A to create a 'molecular glue' that blocks RAS.
The FDA has already fast-tracked the drug for approval and last week permitted drugmaker Revolution Medicines to provide it to patients outside clinical trials via an expanded access program.
The Phase 3 trial included patients without the KRAS mutation, suggesting potentially all pancreatic cancer patients might benefit. Only 3% of patients with metastatic disease survive five years.

stories.headline: ECB Signals Rate Hike Likely as Hormuz Crisis Pushes Eurozone Inflation to 3%, Oil Could Hit $145

key_facts.fact: ECB board member Piero Cipollone said in a May 6 speech in Milan that the chance of a rate hike has risen, stating 'the current situation seems to be drifting away from our March baseline projections, which increases the likelihood that we may need to adjust our policy rates.'
Eurozone headline inflation rose to 3% in April, driven by a 10.9% increase in energy prices, while inflation excluding energy fell to 2.2%.

The ECB's severe scenario models oil prices peaking at $145/barrel and gas at €106/MWh in Q2 2026, which would push inflation cumulatively 6.3 percentage points higher through 2028 than December projections.
The net decline in global oil supply from the Iran war is estimated at around 12 million barrels per day (~11% of prewar supply), larger than the 1973, 1979, and 2022 crises combined.
Cipollone warned Europe could start running out of jet fuel and kerosene reserves by end of May, potentially leading to restrictions 'akin to those seen during the COVID-19 pandemic.'

Financial markets expect three ECB rate hikes, with the first fully priced in by July. Negotiated wage growth remains at 2.6% through end-2026, suggesting workers have yet to demand compensation for the inflation surge.

stories.headline: France Deploys Charles de Gaulle Carrier to Red Sea, Leads 40+ Nation Hormuz Coalition

key_facts.fact: France is deploying the Charles de Gaulle nuclear aircraft carrier strike group through the Suez Canal on May 6 into the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden, positioning for a possible mission to secure navigation in the Strait of Hormuz.
France and the UK are leading a group of more than 40 countries drawing up plans to restore navigation in the Strait of Hormuz; the initiative would be strictly defensive.

The carrier group includes 20 Rafale jets, two E-2C Hawkeye airborne early warning aircraft, and three helicopters. France is the only country besides the US to operate a nuclear carrier with catapult launch systems.

Macron has said the multinational initiative would only begin once the hottest phase of the conflict subsides; the pre-positioning is to reduce delay in launching the operation when circumstances permit.
The Netherlands said its air-defense frigate Evertsen has left the carrier group and is returning to Den Helder.

stories.headline: Google Releases Multi-Token Prediction Drafters for Gemma 4, Up to 3x Faster Inference

key_facts.fact: Google released Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) drafters for its Gemma 4 open-weight models, using speculative decoding to deliver up to 3x faster inference without any degradation in output quality or reasoning logic.

MTP drafters are smaller auxiliary models that predict several tokens at once while the main model waits for data; the main model then verifies all suggestions in a single pass, eliminating idle GPU cycles caused by memory bandwidth bottlenecks.
The speedup works across smartphones, local computers, and cloud applications; MTP drafters are available under the open Apache 2.0 license on Hugging Face and Kaggle.
Gemma 4, introduced in early April and built on the same technology as Google's Gemini AI, has already been downloaded over 60 million times.
Google is also working to optimize Gemma 4 models of different weights for specific hardware such as Apple Silicon and NVIDIA A100 accelerators.

stories.headline: Hut 8 Signs $9.8B 15-Year Lease for 352MW AI Data Center in Texas, Total Contracted Value Hits $16.8B

key_facts.fact: Hut 8 signed a 15-year, $9.8B triple-net lease for 352MW of IT capacity at its Beacon Point campus in Nueces County, Texas, with an unnamed high-investment-grade tenant.
With three 5-year renewal options, the contract value could reach approximately $25.1B. The lease includes a 3.0% annual base rent escalator.
The facility will be designed to NVIDIA's DSX reference architecture for gigawatt-scale AI infrastructure. Initial data hall delivery is expected in Q3 2027.
Beacon Point is the second campus under Hut 8's power-first model, following River Bend. Total contracted AI data center capacity is now 597MW with aggregate base-term value of ~$16.8B.
Hut 8 has an interconnection agreement for 1,000MW of utility capacity at the site, with initial energization expected in Q1 2027. Roughly half the campus remains available for future deals.
Hut 8 stock jumped the most since 2021 on the announcement. The company also closed a $3.25B offering of investment-grade senior secured notes for the River Bend project.

stories.headline: Microsoft Weighs Delaying or Dropping 2030 Hourly Clean Energy Target Amid Data Center Boom

key_facts.fact: Microsoft is considering delaying or abandoning its 2030 '100/100/0' target of matching 100% of its hourly electricity use with zero-carbon energy purchases on the same grid.
The hourly matching goal, announced in 2021, is considerably more ambitious than Microsoft's already-met annual matching target. Internal discussions are ongoing with no final decision.
Microsoft has already begun reducing its carbon-dioxide removal program. The company's carbon emissions have risen 23% since late 2022.
Microsoft is spending ~$190B on data centers through end of 2026. Last month, it announced working with Chevron and Engine No. 1 on a natural gas plant in West Texas that could generate up to 5 GW.
A Microsoft spokesperson pointed to recently signed agreements with We Energies to bring 1.2 GW of carbon-free energy projects in Wisconsin onto the grid, starting in December 2028.

stories.headline: Moonshot AI Raises ~$2B at $20B+ Valuation Led by Meituan, ARR Tops $200M

key_facts.fact: Chinese AI startup Moonshot AI, maker of the Kimi chatbot, raised approximately $2 billion in a new funding round at a post-money valuation above $20 billion, led by Meituan's Dragon Ball venture arm.
Meituan Dragon Ball alone contributed over $200 million, with participation from China Mobile and CITIC Private Equity Funds (CPE).
Moonshot's valuation has more than quadrupled from ~$4.3 billion in November 2025 to over $20 billion; cumulative fundraising exceeds $3.9 billion in less than six months and $5.5 billion total.
Moonshot's annual recurring revenue doubled from $100 million in early March to over $200 million in April 2026, driven by paid subscriptions and enterprise API calls.
Moonshot released and open-sourced its K2.6 model in April, which features enhanced coding capabilities and supports the collaboration of up to 300 sub-agents.
Founded by former Tsinghua University professor Yang Zhilin, Moonshot faces intense talent competition and plans to significantly boost employee stock option incentives this year.

stories.headline: Nvidia Invests $500M in Corning Warrants; Corning to Build 3 US Plants and Expand Optical Capacity 10x

key_facts.fact: Nvidia purchased $500M in Corning share rights: warrants to buy up to 15 million shares at $180 each, plus a pre-funded warrant for up to 3 million shares at $0.0001 each.
Corning will increase U.S.-based optical connectivity manufacturing capacity by 10x and expand domestic fiber production capacity by more than 50%.
Corning will build three new advanced manufacturing facilities in North Carolina and Texas, creating more than 3,000 high-paying American jobs.
Nvidia is likely preparing to replace copper with Corning's optical fibers in its rack-scale AI systems via co-packaged optics, which Jensen Huang called essential at GTC 2025.
Corning shares climbed 12-19% on the news; Nvidia stock gained almost 6%. Corning raised its long-term sales target to a $20B annualized run rate by end of 2026, $30B by 2028, and $40B by 2030.
The deal extends Nvidia's pattern from March 2026, when it invested $4B across Coherent and Lumentum, the two principal laser-component suppliers for its co-packaged optics platform.

stories.headline: Roche Agrees to Acquire PathAI for Up to $1.05B to Transform AI-Driven Diagnostics

key_facts.fact: Swiss pharmaceutical giant Roche agreed to acquire US-based PathAI, which makes AI-powered digital pathology tools, for up to $1.05 billion — $750 million upfront with up to $300 million in milestone-based payments.
The acquisition builds on a partnership established in 2021 and expanded in 2024 to include development of AI-enabled companion diagnostic algorithms; the deal is expected to close in H2 2026.
PathAI's AISight Image Management System software integrates advanced AI analysis and workflow capabilities for digital pathology labs, enabling automated processing of high-resolution tissue images.

Roche Diagnostics CEO Matt Sause said the deal will combine PathAI's digital pathology tools with Roche's oncology diagnosis platforms to improve precision cancer diagnosis and potentially better patient outcomes.
PathAI will become part of Roche's Diagnostics division; Roche intends to scale PathAI's solutions globally and strengthen its biopharma services for precision medicine.

stories.headline: Samsung Unions Threaten 18-Day Strike Starting May 21 Over AI Chip Profit Sharing

key_facts.fact: Two Samsung Electronics unions are demanding the company pay 15% of each division's operating profits to workers and raise wages by 7%. They threaten an 18-day walkout starting May 21.
Samsung management offered ~13% of operating profit to chip division staff and special rewards exceeding the OPI upper limit if DS Division achieves top position in domestic sales and profit.
Samsung reported record Q1 2026 results: sales of KRW 133.9T (up 69% YoY) and operating profit of KRW 57.2T (up 756%), surpassing 2025's full-year operating profit in one quarter.
Samsung Vice Chairman Jeon Younghyun and President Noh Taemun urged employees not to compromise future competitiveness, warning the global business environment is challenging.
Board Chairman Shin Je-yoon warned a strike could cause losses of up to KRW 1T per day at semiconductor plants and reduce operating profit by up to KRW 10T if prolonged.
The Bank of Korea estimates about half of Korea's Q1 GDP growth of 1.7% was attributable to chipmaking. Samsung and SK Hynix account for over 40% of the Kospi index value.

stories.headline: Scale AI Wins $500M Pentagon Contract, Five Times Its Previous $100M Deal

key_facts.fact: The Pentagon awarded Scale AI a $500 million contract to help sift through data and assist in military decision-making, a five-fold increase from its $100 million deal signed in September 2025.
The contract was signed with the Pentagon's Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Office (CDAO), the principal procurement vehicle for US military AI integration spending.
Dan Tadross, who leads Scale AI's public sector business, said the Pentagon was 'pushing the limits' on the original contract and the deal shows the department is 'eager to adopt this technology.'

Scale AI participates in the Defense Innovation Unit's Thunderforge programme and Trump's Golden Dome homeland defense framework, and its Scale Donovan platform deploys AI agents on networks classified up to Top Secret.
Meta holds a 49% equity stake in Scale AI; the company developed Defense Llama, a national-security language model built on Meta's Llama 3 framework, for classified government deployment.

stories.headline: MEMS Foundry Silex Surges 127% in Stockholm IPO Debut, Strongest European Chip Listing in Five Years

key_facts.fact: Silex Microsystems debuted on Nasdaq Stockholm on May 7, with shares surging up to 127% above the IPO price of SEK 81 per share. The offering was oversubscribed several times.
The IPO raised approximately SEK 2.0B (~$220M) on a 24.6 million share offering, with a post-IPO valuation of SEK 8.9B. Proceeds split between 12.35M newly issued shares and 12.25M existing shares.
Bloomberg called it the strongest open for a sizable European IPO in almost five years. Cornerstone investors including Capital Research, Fidelity, and Swedish pension funds took ~75% of shares.

Silex is the world's leading pure-play MEMS foundry, manufacturing micro-electromechanical systems for automotive, industrial, life sciences, and consumer electronics from a single fab near Stockholm.
Silex reported 2025 revenue of SEK 1.385B with EBIT of SEK 368M (~27% operating margin). Q1 2026 was stronger: SEK 375M revenue and SEK 128M EBIT (~34% operating margin).
Silex's Chinese shareholder Sai MicroElectronics sold existing shares as part of the offering. The IPO welcomed 14,000 new shareholders.

stories.headline: Anthropic Signs Deal for All of SpaceX's Colossus 1: 220,000+ NVIDIA GPUs and 300MW of Capacity

key_facts.fact: Anthropic signed a deal to use all compute capacity at SpaceX's Colossus 1 data center in Memphis, gaining access to 220,000+ NVIDIA GPUs (H100, H200, GB200) and 300MW of new capacity within the month.
Anthropic also expressed interest in partnering with SpaceX to develop multiple gigawatts of orbital AI compute capacity, citing terrestrial power, land, and cooling constraints.
Musk reversed his stance on Anthropic, saying he spent time with their team and was 'impressed.' In February he had called Anthropic 'misanthropic' and said Claude 'hates Western Civilization.'
Musk confirmed xAI 'will be dissolved as a separate company' and will be called SpaceXAI. SpaceX has moved its AI training to Colossus 2.
The deal adds to Anthropic's growing stack of compute agreements: up to 5GW with Amazon, 5GW with Google/Broadcom, $30B Azure capacity with Microsoft/Nvidia, and $50B US AI infra with Fluidstack.
Reports have highlighted that xAI was only utilizing ~11% of its installed compute resources due to unoptimized software stacks, freeing capacity for the Anthropic lease.
The deal arrives weeks before SpaceX's planned IPO targeting a $1.75T-$2T valuation, with the public S-1 expected by late May and roadshow set for the week of June 8.

stories.headline: UN Security Council Holds Emergency Session After Iran Launches 12 Ballistic Missiles at UAE

key_facts.fact: The UN Security Council held a closed-door meeting on May 6 focused on Iranian missile and drone attacks on the UAE on Monday, briefed by Under-Secretary-General Rosemary DiCarlo.

The UAE Ambassador said Iran launched 12 ballistic missiles, 3 cruise missiles, and 4 UAVs at the UAE, striking the Fujairah oil industry zone and injuring 3 civilians. Most threats were intercepted by UAE air defenses.
Since the crisis began on February 28, the UAE has intercepted over 500 ballistic missiles, nearly 30 cruise missiles, and more than 2,000 UAVs launched from Iran.
The International Maritime Organization confirmed 32 maritime incidents and 10 fatalities to date, including an attack on French vessel San Antonio on May 5 that injured 8 seafarers.

The emergency session was requested by Bahrain, which called the attacks a 'clear violation' of Security Council resolution 2817 (2026) adopted in March after Iranian attacks on neighboring countries.

stories.headline: US and Iran Close In on 14-Point MOU to End War; Iran Expected to Reply Thursday

key_facts.fact: The US presented a one-page, 14-point memorandum of understanding to Iran that would declare an end to the war and trigger a 30-day negotiation period on nuclear issues, unfreezing assets, and Hormuz security.
Iran is expected to give mediators its reply to the proposal on Thursday, according to a regional source.
The MOU includes discussion of a moratorium on uranium enrichment for longer than 10 years and requires Iran to ship its stockpile of highly enriched uranium out of the country.

Trump said the US has had 'very good talks with Iran in the last 24 hours' and that a deal is possible, but also threatened that if Iran doesn't agree, 'the bombing starts' at 'a much higher level and intensity.'

US Central Command shot at and disabled an Iranian-flagged oil tanker M/T Hasna in the Gulf of Oman on May 6 after it attempted to violate the US blockade, using 20mm cannon fire from an F/A-18 Super Hornet launched from USS Abraham Lincoln.
Iranian foreign ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei said the US proposal 'is still being reviewed by Iran' and after finalizing its viewpoints, Iran will convey them to the Pakistani mediators.
A senior member of Iran's parliament dismissed the proposal as a 'wish list' and said Iran 'has its finger on the trigger and is ready' to deliver a 'harsh response' if the US does not 'surrender.'
